title: Seven bridges, each crossed once – is it possible?
description:
The river Pregel split Königsberg into four parts, linked by seven bridges. Is there a walk that crosses every bridge exactly once? Leonhard Euler called the puzzle banal – then proved in 1735, with dots and lines, that it can't be done. The birth of graph theory.

One true story from the history of math – every day.
Created with AI assistance (animation and voice); facts from the sources listed.

Sources:
· L. Euler, Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (vorgelegt 1735, gedruckt 1741)
· T. Paoletti, Leonard Euler's Solution to the Königsberg Bridge Problem (MAA Convergence)
· I. Peterson, Euler's Bridges (Science News, 2006)
